title: Develop against the active bishop
summary: Develop behind the pawn centre without ignoring the bishop already outside Black's chain.

fromNode.nodeId: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5

goal: Develop behind the pawn centre without ignoring the bishop already outside Black's chain.

steps.text: Develop the king-side knight to support the central pawns.
Bring out the king-side bishop and prepare to castle when safe.
Develop the remaining pieces while checking central captures and the active opposing bishop.

jobs.text: Keep the pawn on e5 coordinated with the other pieces; check threats before moving it again.
The pawn controls e5 from here.
The queen controls d4 from here.

opponent.text: The bishop on f5 is already outside the pawn chain. Black can still challenge the centre with the c-pawn; do not ignore that break while developing.

notNow: Do not copy a French plan that assumes the opposing light-square bishop is blocked on c8.

mistakes.text: The bishop on h6 can be taken by the pawn on g7. Do not sacrifice a developed piece without a concrete follow-up.

comments.text: Develop the king-side knight to support d4 and e5. The opposing light-square bishop is already outside the pawn chain, so do not treat this as the same French position.
Bring your bishop to e2. It supports your knight on f3.
Bring your bishop to e3. From e3 it controls d4. Keep watching Black's replies before advancing more pawns.
Capture the pawn with your knight. From d4 it attacks the bishop on f5; an attack is not a guarantee of winning it.
Bring your pawn to c4. From c4 it controls d5. Keep watching Black's replies before advancing more pawns.
Bring your queen to a4. From a4 it attacks the knight on c6; an attack is not a guarantee of winning it.
